checks.note: The page quotes 'Android OS 9 or later', says HD needs Widevine L1, and says L3 means SD. It also warns that rooted or modified devices 'might not be able to download' the app, and that changes to certification status 'may keep the Netflix app from functioning properly'. The plans page confirms Standard with ads and Standard at 1080p, and Premium at 4K + HDR.

checks.claim: The Netflix Android TV app (com.netflix.ninja) does not work on uncertified devices; workarounds are not recommended.
checks.note: Netflix's -13 article: 'If you do not see the Netflix app in the Google Play Store, your device is not compatible with Netflix.' In the Khadas VIM4 thread (Aug 2023) the TV app fails with -13. androidpctv says the TV app 'does not work because the DRM protection'. The aidanmacgregor repo does embed an ESN, and its ESN history says one was blocked 'after several months' and another 'a week or so later'. The repo does not say the ESN is 'borrowed', and it lists an Android 12+ issue. The CastagnaIT README confirms development is 'SUSPENDED' and playback 'WHEN IT WORKS, IS LIMITED TO SD'. The BadBox firmware does spoof ADT-3 and lists Netflix_425.apk (com.netflix.ninja) for install.

checks.claim: The sideloaded phone/tablet Netflix app runs on H713 projectors without Google Play at about 540p, stereo.
checks.note: The HY300 Pro review gives Netflix 540p SD, stereo, with apps installed from APK and no Google Play. androidpctv's guide says '960x540p or more' for the latest version. The L018 review gives SD. PCWelt (15 May 2017) confirms that the 2017 block was a Play-listing block and that APK installs kept working. The Trusted Reviews article was not opened.

checks.claim: The Netflix phone app does not need Google Play Services or Play Integrity at runtime; the gate is the Play listing.
checks.note: Supported indirectly: the review units have no Play and still play Netflix. An androidayuda piece (about Nov 2025, judging by its image path) says the app 'continues to function normally' on rooted devices but that Netflix 'may strengthen its controls'. Fastweb confirms you cannot subscribe inside an app without GMS, so sign up on the web. The GrapheneOS threads would not load. Their content was seen only in search snippets: the app works installed outside Play, and the listing declares a SafetyNet/Integrity requirement. That is user-reported, undated, and not confirmed by Netflix. I found no 2025-2026 source on runtime enforcement either way, so this is absence of evidence. Netflix's own page keeps a hedge for rooted devices.

checks.claim: 32-bit armeabi-v7a is supported by Netflix 8.x builds; for 9.x builds it could not be confirmed.
checks.note: The gap is narrower than stated. APKMirror search results show Netflix 9.26.0 as armeabi-v7a, Android 9.0+, nodpi, dated 6 Aug 2025. They also show 9.38.0 as com.netflix.mediaclient_9.38.0-63520_minAPI28(armeabi-v7a)(nodpi), signed by Netflix, Inc. APKMirror pages return 403 to my fetches, so this rests on search snippets only. The newest 2026 builds (for example 9.87.1 build 9, nodpi) have no architecture shown, so 32-bit support for current 2026 builds is still not confirmed.

checks.claim: Using the phone Netflix app on a projector needs a D-pad helper or an air mouse.
checks.note: The BadBox writeup confirms com.android.nfx at /system/priv-app/NFXAccessibility. It is a 'Netflix D-pad navigation helper, active only while com.netflix.mediaclient is in the foreground', its manifest has no INTERNET permission, and the analyst 'kept, harmless'. It does not list the helper's other permissions, and an accessibility service is powerful, so 'harmless' is the analyst's judgement. androidpctv says 'we are going to need a mouse or fly mouse'. The ManoMano buyer review was not checked.

checks.claim: In one H713 firmware family the malware drops the Widevine L3 bundle, so Widevine may break after cleanup.
checks.note: The fact is confirmed: plugin.jar 'drops a DRM key/licence bundle so streaming apps run on the uncertified device' into /data/mediadrm/IDM1013/L3/, downloaded as L3.zip from a URL with 'rk3326' in its path (the doc treats that as a label only). Neodyme shows that /data/vendor/mediadrm/IDM1013/L3/ is the normal Widevine L3 storage directory, holding the encrypted keybox. KeyDive's developer docs say L3 devices may use a 'pre-installed baked-in DRM certificate'. So the drop plausibly plants keybox or certificate material. Whether removing it breaks Widevine on the HY320 cannot be verified. The consequence is a hypothesis.

checks.claim: Disney+ plays at about 720p on H713 L3 units; the sideloaded APK works; Google-services dependence is mixed.
checks.note: 720p is confirmed by both reviews ('HD (720p)' and 'Disney+ caps at 720p'). androidpctv's Disney+ article (2020, updated 2022) confirms Play hides the app on uncertified boxes and that a manual APK install works. The GrapheneOS thread would not load, so the mixed reports are unverified. ARM v7 support was 'not found' in the research, but APKMirror search snippets show the phone build Disney+ 26.15.2+rc1-2026.09.01 (Android 6.0+) with an armeabi-v7a split.

checks.claim: Prime Video plays at SD (480p) on H713 L3; Amazon Appstore for Android closed 20 Aug 2025.
checks.note: The HY300 Pro review gives 480p SD, stereo. The L018 review gives SD. The Appstore shutdown on 20 Aug 2025 was for Android phones and tablets only, with Fire devices unaffected, and Amazon gives no guarantee that apps installed from it keep working. Extra: APKMirror snippets show the phone app com.amazon.avod.thirdpartyclient 3.0.459.345 as arm-v7a, Android 9.0+ (June 2026).

checks.claim: SmartTube: no Google services needed, armeabi-v7a builds, get it only from GitHub or F-Droid because of the Dec 2025 key compromise (30.43-30.47, 30.51; 30.55+ new key).
checks.note: Confirmed: the README says 'Does not require Google Services', Android 4.3+, 'Do not download SmartTube from any app store, APK websites or blogs', F-Droid package app.smarttube.fdroid, and the kutt.to links. Releases show stable 32.56 (23 Sep) and beta 32.68 (17 Oct) with armeabi-v7a APKs. The affected range is understated. BleepingComputer gives the developer's estimate of 30.43-30.47, with 30.51 found infected by a user. AhnLab says the malicious library 'has been included since version 30.27'. CyberInsider says 'versions between 28.56 and 30.52' were most affected, and that 30.56 uses a new key and 'installs as a separate application due to the changed package name'. BleepingComputer has the developer saying 30.55+ uses the new key. The claim about the official YouTube TV app needing Google services was not verified.

checks.claim: RaiPlay: no evidence on its Google Play Services or Widevine-level needs on uncertified devices.
checks.note: This is a 'not found' claim. I did not find any source either. It has to be tested on the device.

checks.claim: microG is possible on rooted Android 11 but gives no streaming benefit and adds risk; skip it.
checks.note: The microG wiki confirms: FakeGApps (whew-inc fork) supports Android 4.0-15, JingMatrix LSPosed 8.1-16, and patchers work properly only below Android 9. AOSP says 'Plugins are built by vendors or SOC makers and put in a /vendor partition', which supports the point that Widevine is not a GMS component. Play Integrity: a rooted or hooked device gets an empty deviceRecognitionVerdict. An uncertified but unrooted device can still get the opt-in MEETS_BASIC_INTEGRITY. Android Police (Mar 2018) confirms the sign-in block on uncertified devices, but the exemption registers the GSF ID, not the 'Android ID'. The Sailfish post is one user's 'as far as I know'. The 2021 Reddit FakeGApps report was not checked.

checks.claim: Netflix through a Chromecast into HDMI is far better: certified, 1080p or 4K up to the panel's limit, TV interface, remote, 5.1/Atmos.
checks.note: The specs are confirmed. Google's spec page gives the HD model up to 1080p HDR and the 4K model 4K, Dolby Vision. Netflix's Chromecast page lists 5.1 and Dolby Atmos for Chromecast with Google TV, and says UHD needs HDCP 2.2. But the research's own cited sources did not contain the 'Google says' resolution statement. More importantly, the user never said they own a Chromecast. Chromecast with Google TV was discontinued (announced Aug 2024, removed from Google Store Feb 2025; one report says security updates ran only until Sep 2025), and the replacement is the Google TV Streamer. Since Nov 2025 Netflix no longer allows casting from a phone to Chromecast with Google TV or Google TV Streamer, so you must use the device's own Netflix app and remote. Older cast-only Chromecasts keep casting, reportedly not on ad plans. HDCP on the H713 HDMI input remains undocumented.

verify.corrected_bottom_line: The core finding stands. H713 projectors are uncertified and Widevine L3, so the sideloaded Netflix phone app plays at about 540p SD, Disney+ at about 720p and Prime Video at about 480p. The Netflix Android TV app will not run without risky ESN mods that Netflix keeps blocking, and microG cannot help. Check the HY320's actual level in Netflix: My Netflix > Menu > App Settings > Diagnostics > Playback Specification. Do it before and after the cleanup. Corrections: (1) 32-bit is less of a worry than stated. Netflix 9.26.0 (Aug 2025) and 9.38.0 have armeabi-v7a builds, and so do recent Disney+ phone builds (Sep 2026) and Prime Video phone builds (June 2026). Whether the very latest Netflix builds still do is unconfirmed. (2) SmartTube's compromised range is wider than 30.43-30.47. AhnLab says since 30.27, CyberInsider says 28.56-30.52. Install only a current release (30.56+ on the new key, new package name; today 32.56 stable) from GitHub releases or F-Droid, and remove any old-package SmartTube. (3) The Chromecast advice assumes hardware the user hasn't mentioned. If they have a Chromecast with Google TV, use its own Netflix app and remote: Netflix removed phone casting to it in Nov 2025. If they have none, the choice is SD Netflix on the projector or a certified streamer (Chromecast with Google TV is discontinued; the Google TV Streamer replaced it). (4) The iPad AirPlay path cannot carry Netflix: Netflix dropped AirPlay in 2019, and the UxPlay-based receiver does not support DRM content. Only YouTube HLS and unprotected content work through it. Widevine breaking after the cleanup is still a hypothesis to test, not a fact.

gaps.issue: The user has not said they own a Chromecast. The recommendation to keep DRM services on the Chromecast depends on that. If they own one, its model matters too: Google TV HD or 4K versus cast-only, because casting rules differ since Nov 2025.

AirPlay from the iPad is not a way around DRM. Netflix removed AirPlay support in 2019. UxPlay says Apple video DRM 'cannot be decrypted', and its HLS mode supports only YouTube. The Android AirPlay Server README says DRM content is not supported. Whether Disney+ and Prime Video are blocked through mirroring was not tested.

APK provenance for Netflix, Disney+ and Prime Video, given the security goal. With no Play Store, the APKs come from a third-party mirror (APKMirror). Before installing over Wi-Fi ADB, compare each APK's signing-certificate fingerprint (apksigner verify --print-certs) with a known-good copy. No official non-Play download channel was found for these apps.

Widevine data location. The BadBox drop path is /data/mediadrm/IDM1013/L3/, but on Android 11 with a vendor Widevine HAL the normal path is /data/vendor/mediadrm/IDM1013/L3/. Back up both before the cleanup. Whether the HY320 firmware plants Widevine material (and so needs it) is unknown.

Identity spoofing. If the HY320 firmware, like the BadBox AT-M269, reports a fake model such as ADT-3 to pass certification, restoring real build properties during the cleanup may change how Netflix and other apps behave. Check getprop ro.product.model / ro.product.manufacturer before and after.

Root and Netflix. Netflix's help page warns that rooted or modified devices may not work properly. No 2025-2026 report of runtime root detection was found, but the Magisk root the plan calls for is a standing risk to Netflix working. Test Netflix playback after rooting.

Phone builds versus Android TV builds. APKMirror marks Prime Video and Disney+ Android TV builds as requiring Android TV. Whether the HY320 firmware declares the leanback feature, and so which build line will install, is unknown. The phone builds are the safe default.
Native panel resolution is still unsettled for this unit. Listings disagree: Magcubic HY320 is given as 1920x1080 native, while other HY320 listings say 720p. It caps SmartTube and any HDMI source.

Not verified: whether the official YouTube Android TV app needs Google services on an uncertified box, whether Netflix 2026 builds (9.7x-9.8x) still ship armeabi-v7a, the RaiPlay and Mediaset Infinity behaviour, and whether the H713 HDMI input supports HDCP 2.2.

research.bottom_line:
Recommended path (most robust on an Android 11 TV build): keep classic TCP ADB, but force RSA key authentication. First pre-authorize the PC's key while you still have root access. Then set ro.adb.secure=1 with a small Magisk module, stop the authorized key from expiring, and install with `adb install` after checking each APK with apksigner on the PC. With this in place, a stranger on the LAN gets only an "unauthorized" connection and an on-screen "Allow USB debugging?" prompt, which you deny. No shell. The remaining risk is that legacy ADB traffic is unencrypted, so an attacker already on your LAN could eavesdrop or tamper in transit (AOSP's own docs say this). Encrypted TLS wireless debugging exists in the Android 11 framework and adbd. Google documents it for TV only on Android 13+, though, and the Android 11 TV Settings app has no pairing screen. You can drive it from the shell (`settings put global adb_wifi_enabled 1` plus the pre-seeded key), but it turns itself off when the Wi-Fi network/BSSID changes and uses a random port. Treat it as an optional upgrade, not the default. Fallbacks if you want ADB off entirely: LocalSend (open source, but its Android TV remote handling is buggy), Material Files pulling from an SMB/SFTP share, or the USB stick.

EXACT FLOW (PowerShell on the PC with Google platform-tools and build-tools; do step 1 while you still have the root access used for rooting, ideally over the USB A-A cable):
1) Pre-seed the PC key (so you cannot lock yourself out):
   adb push $env:USERPROFILE\.android\adbkey.pub /data/local/tmp/pc.pub
   adb shell "su -c 'cat /data/local/tmp/pc.pub >> /data/misc/adb/adb_keys; chown system:shell /data/misc/adb/adb_keys; chmod 0640 /data/misc/adb/adb_keys; restorecon /data/misc/adb/adb_keys; rm /data/local/tmp/pc.pub'"
   adb shell settings put global adb_allowed_connection_time 0    (stops the framework from removing the key after 7 days without use)
2) Enforce authentication with a Magisk module /data/adb/modules/adbsecure/ (module.prop plus system.prop containing the line: ro.adb.secure=1). Leave persist.adb.tcp.port=5555 as it is if you want Wi-Fi installs. Reboot.
3) Verify:
   adb kill-server; adb connect <ip>:5555; adb devices  -> "device"
   adb shell getprop ro.adb.secure -> 1
   Negative test: stop the server, rename %USERPROFILE%\.android to .android.bak, connect again. Expect "unauthorized" and an on-screen prompt; deny it. Then stop the server, delete the new .android and rename the backup back.
   Also scan the projector's ports from the PC to confirm only the expected listeners are open.
4) Each install:
   apksigner verify --print-certs -v app.apk   -> must print "Verifies"; compare the "Signer #1 certificate SHA-256 digest" with the developer's or F-Droid's published value (lowercase, no colons)
   adb connect <ip>:5555
   adb install -r app.apk      (pick the armeabi-v7a or universal APK)
   adb disconnect <ip>:5555
Optional hardening: give the projector a fixed IP via a DHCP reservation on the router. Turn "USB debugging" off in Developer options between sessions, and confirm with a port scan that 5555 actually closes (not verified for this firmware). Optional upgrade to TLS: `adb shell settings put global adb_wifi_enabled 1`, accept the "Allow wireless debugging on this network / Always allow" dialog, read the port with `adb shell getprop service.adb.tls.port` or `adb mdns services`, then `adb connect <ip>:<tlsport>`. After that you can remove persist.adb.tcp.port, but check the is_usb fallback described below first.

findings.claim: Google documents wireless debugging (adb pair) for TV devices only on Android 13+. Phones get it on Android 11+.
findings.detail: developer.android.com/tools/adb lists the prerequisite as 'Android 11 (API 30) or higher for phones, or Android 13 (API 33) or higher for TV and Wear OS'. The flow is: Developer options > Wireless debugging > 'Pair using pairing code' (6-digit code, IP, port) > `adb pair ip:port` > enter the code. Pairing happens once, and the device stays paired until you choose Forget or revoke authorizations. QR pairing means the device scans a QR code shown by Android Studio, which is impossible on a projector with no camera. My inference, not confirmed in a source: the 13+ limit for TV is because the Android 11 TvSettings app has no Wireless debugging screen. I could not fetch the TvSettings source to check this.

findings.claim: The Android 11 framework does contain TLS wireless debugging, and setting Settings.Global adb_wifi_enabled=1 starts it without the Settings UI.
findings.detail: AdbService (android11-release) registers a ContentObserver on ADB_WIFI_ENABLED and calls setAdbEnabled(shouldEnable, AdbTransportType.WIFI). AdbDebuggingManager then gets the current AP, runs verifyWifiNetwork(), sets persist.adb.tls_server.enable=1, and polls service.adb.tls.port, a random port it waits up to 10 s for. So `adb shell settings put global adb_wifi_enabled 1` works, because the shell user can write global settings. Pairing is the hard part. The 6-digit code is generated by SecureRandom and broadcast for a UI to display. enablePairingByPairingCode / enablePairingByQrCode require MANAGE_DEBUGGING, and I found no shell command that shows the code. Without a pairing UI, use the pre-seeded-key route in the next finding.

findings.claim: Being 'paired' just means the host's public key is in /data/misc/adb/adb_keys. A key you add there yourself, or one accepted with 'Always allow', should therefore also work for TLS connections without running adb pair.
findings.detail: The AOSP adb_wifi.md doc says a host and device are 'paired if the host's public key is in the device's /data/misc/adb/adb_keys or /adb_keys files'. adbd's TLS check (adbd_tls_verify_cert) compares the client certificate's key against the same key set (adbd_auth_get_public_keys) used for legacy RSA auth, and a successful pairing writes the key into adb_keys. Not tested on this firmware. Also, mDNS auto-connect relies on a GUID learned during pairing, so you have to type `adb connect ip:tlsport` manually.

findings.claim: Wireless debugging turns itself off when Wi-Fi drops or the BSSID changes. Network trust is stored per BSSID, and a network that is not trusted triggers an on-screen confirmation dialog.
findings.detail: In the AdbDebuggingManager broadcast receiver, Wi-Fi disabled, a disconnect, an empty BSSID, or a BSSID different from the stored one ('Detected wifi network change. Disabling adbwifi.') all set ADB_WIFI_ENABLED back to 0. If the device is not on Wi-Fi when it is enabled, the setting is reset to 0. An untrusted BSSID launches SystemUI's .wifi.WifiDebuggingActivity, which the Android 11 SystemUI manifest declares. 'Always allow' stores the BSSID in adb_temp_keys.xml. Inference: on a dual-band router like the home router, each band has its own BSSID, so roaming between bands would switch debugging off and each BSSID needs its own trust. At boot it re-enables from persist.adb.tls_server.enable, but it gets switched off again if Wi-Fi is not connected yet.

findings.claim: How unauthenticated port 5555 happens: adbd skips authentication only on a debuggable build (ro.debuggable=1) or an unlocked device (ro.boot.verifiedbootstate=orange), and then only if ro.adb.secure is 0 or missing. The TCP listener comes from service.adb.tcp.port or persist.adb.tcp.port, or from a fallback to 5555 when there is no USB FFS endpoint.
findings.detail: adbd main.cpp (android11): 'If we're on userdebug/eng or the device is unlocked, permit no-authentication': if (__android_log_is_debuggable() || device_unlocked) auth_required = GetBoolProperty("ro.adb.secure", false). The default is false, so a missing property means no authentication. The port is read from service.adb.tcp.port, then persist.adb.tcp.port. If neither is set and is_usb is false (access(USB_FFS_ADB_EP0) fails), adbd still listens on tcp:DEFAULT_ADB_LOCAL_TRANSPORT_PORT (5555). AOSP's build sets ro.adb.secure=1 only for 'user' builds and ro.debuggable=1 for userdebug/eng. Important consequence: unlocking the bootloader for Magisk can by itself disable authentication if the vendor props lack ro.adb.secure=1, so set it explicitly. A comparable real case is CVE-2026-30495 (Optoma projector: ADB on 5555 with no authentication, ro.adb.secure=0, /system/xbin/su, CVSS 8.8 AV:A).

findings.claim: Setting ro.adb.secure=1 with a Magisk module (system.prop or `resetprop -n` in post-fs-data) should take effect before adbd starts, without editing build.prop on vendor/odm/product.
findings.detail: Magisk: system.prop entries 'will be loaded as system properties by resetprop'. post-fs-data is blocking and runs before Zygote, and you must use `resetprop -n` there, never setprop, which deadlocks. resetprop also offers -p (persistent) and -d/--delete, for example `resetprop -p -d persist.adb.tcp.port` to close the listener. AOSP init.usb.rc starts adbd only from sys.usb.config property triggers set at 'on boot', which comes after post-fs-data. Vendor .rc files could start it earlier, so after boot check `getprop ro.adb.secure` and do the negative test. If authentication is not enforced, add `stop adbd; start adbd` to service.sh. Editing build.prop on vendor/odm/product works too, but it changes partitions (AVB/dm-verity risk). Prefer the Magisk overlay, which you can remove.

findings.claim: Lock-out risk: USB ADB uses the same RSA authentication, so it is not a separate escape route. Pre-seed adb_keys and turn off key expiry before you enforce ro.adb.secure=1.
findings.detail: Legacy adbd sends A_AUTH on every transport. Trusted keys come from /adb_keys and /data/misc/adb/adb_keys, and unknown keys go to a framework prompt (SystemUI .usb.UsbDebuggingActivity). Fire TV's documentation confirms the 'Allow USB debugging?' prompt also appears for `adb connect` over the network. If this vendor's SystemUI lacks that dialog, an un-seeded key cannot be approved over USB or Wi-Fi. Keys you add by hand are kept (addUserKeysToKeyStore), but they expire after ADB_ALLOWED_CONNECTION_TIME (default one week without use) unless the setting is 0. Escape routes: the Magisk app (disable the module), `magisk --remove-modules` (needs working ADB), Magisk Safe Mode (needs a volume-down key at boot, uncertain on a projector), or the HY300-family hardware flash mode (paperclip button above HDMI plus a USB A-A cable) with your full eMMC backup or the stock boot image.

findings.claim: Legacy TCP ADB with RSA authentication is authenticated but unencrypted. TLS wireless debugging is encrypted.
findings.detail: AOSP adb_wifi.md says of the adb tcpip channel: 'all traffic can be eavesdropped and open to MITM attacks'. The legacy socket answers every connection with A_AUTH. The TLS socket starts with A_STLS and encrypts everything. On a home WPA2 LAN, the realistic threat to the legacy path is another device already on the LAN actively intercepting while you are connected. An attacker who only scans gets 'unauthorized'. Limit exposure by keeping ADB off when you are not using it.

findings.claim: LocalSend is a viable open-source way to send APKs without ADB, but it has known problems on Android TV and opens a LAN listener.
findings.detail: F-Droid: Apache-2.0, built and signed by the developer (reproducible), armeabi-v7a APK available, min Android 7.0, version 1.18.2 (Aug 2026). It requests install packages, so it can hand a received APK to the system installer, and you still confirm the install. Protocol: TCP/UDP 53317, multicast 224.0.0.167, HTTPS where the fingerprint is the SHA-256 of a self-signed cert. The receiver accepts or rejects each transfer, an optional PIN is available, and the protocol docs mention no MITM protection. Open TV issues: #249 (the OK button cannot confirm incoming transfers), #1264 (cannot control it with an Android TV remote), #3335 (APK fails to install on an HY350max projector).

findings.claim: Pull-based alternative with no listener on the projector: Material Files (GPL-3.0, built and signed by F-Droid, armeabi-v7a, min Android 6) reads FTP/SFTP/SMB/WebDAV shares and has the install-packages permission.
findings.detail: The trade-off is that the projector stores credentials for the share, so use a dedicated read-only account. Android TV usability is not documented. 'Send Files to TV' (yablio): no source repository found, so I treat it as proprietary and do not recommend it. The USB stick is the zero-network fallback.

findings.claim: How to verify an APK on Windows: `apksigner verify --print-certs -v app.apk` (SDK Build Tools 24.0.3+, under build-tools\<ver>\), then compare 'Signer #1 certificate SHA-256 digest' with the developer's or F-Droid's published value.
findings.detail: apksigner prints lowercase hex without colons, so normalize published fingerprints before comparing. Independent cross-checks for F-Droid APKs: (a) f-droid.org/repo/signer-index.json, the official list of signer SHA-256 values, itself signed via entry.json, signer-index.jar and signer-index.json.asc; (b) `gpg --verify <apk>.asc <apk>` against F-Droid's key 37D2 C987 89D8 3119 4839 4E3E 41E7 044E 1DBA 2E89; (c) for developer-signed reproducible apps such as AirPlay Server (io.github.jqssun.airplay 0.0.31, armeabi-v7a, F-Droid apk and .asc), the cert should equal the one on the GitHub release APK. Android itself then requires every update to carry the same cert. On Windows the wrapper is apksigner.bat and needs a Java runtime; the .bat name and the Java requirement are my own knowledge, not from the docs I fetched.

findings.claim: Because the firmware's platform is signed with AOSP test keys, refuse any third-party APK whose signer is the AOSP test DN.
findings.detail: AOSP's security README says test keys 'should NEVER be used to sign packages in publicly released images' and gives their DN as /C=US/ST=California/L=Mountain View/O=Android/OU=Android/CN=Android/emailAddress=android@android.com. Inference: if this device's platform cert is the public test key, any APK signed with that key can get platform/system privileges. If apksigner shows that DN, do not install the APK.

findings.claim: Optional on-demand switch: a Magisk module can include action.sh, which runs when you press the module's Action button in the Magisk app, for example to set or clear service.adb.tcp.port and restart adbd.
findings.detail: Magisk guides: action.sh 'will be executed when user click the action button in Magisk app'. Because of the is_usb fallback, clearing the port does not close 5555 if /dev/usb-ffs/adb/ep0 is missing. Stopping adbd, or turning USB debugging off, is what reliably closes it. Not tested; check with a port scan.

open_questions: What the projector actually reports: getprop ro.build.type, ro.debuggable, ro.boot.verifiedbootstate, ro.adb.secure, persist.adb.tcp.port, service.adb.tcp.port. Also which file or .rc sets them (grep the /system/etc/prop.default, /vendor, /odm and /product build.prop files, plus /vendor/etc/init and /system/etc/init for 'adb').

Whether this vendor's SystemUI includes .usb.UsbDebuggingActivity and .wifi.WifiDebuggingActivity (adb shell pm dump com.android.systemui, look for 'Debugging'). If either is missing, the prompts never appear and the pre-seeded key is mandatory.
Whether /dev/usb-ffs/adb/ep0 exists. If not, adbd always falls back to TCP 5555 when no port property is set.
Whether the vendor's TV settings have a working 'USB debugging' toggle that really stops adbd, closing 5555 (check with a port scan).
Not tested here: connecting over TLS (adb connect ip:service.adb.tls.port) with a key pre-seeded in adb_keys, without running adb pair, on this Android 11 build.
Whether the Magisk app (and its module Action button) can be operated with the projector's remote, and whether Magisk Safe Mode can be triggered at all without a hardware volume key.
Exact menu path for a DHCP reservation on the home router. Not researched.

checks.claim: Google documents wireless debugging (adb pair) for TV only on Android 13+, phones on Android 11+. Pairing is done once and lasts until you Forget it or revoke. QR pairing needs the device to scan a code.
checks.note: The adb page says: 'Android 11 (API level 30) or higher for phone or Android 13 (API level 33) or higher for TV and WearOS'. The pairing-code steps, the once-only pairing, Forget and Revoke all match. QR pairing is only described as the device scanning a code shown by Android Studio. The research's own guess (the Android 11 TvSettings app has no Wireless debugging screen) remains unverifiable: I found no TvSettings source or Android TV release note.

checks.claim: The Android 11 framework contains TLS wireless debugging, and `settings put global adb_wifi_enabled 1` starts it without the Settings UI. The pairing APIs need MANAGE_DEBUGGING.
checks.note: AdbService (android11-release) watches ADB_WIFI_ENABLED and calls setAdbEnabled(..., WIFI). AdbDebuggingManager then runs verifyWifiNetwork, sets persist.adb.tls_server.enable=1, and polls service.adb.tls.port for 10 s. enablePairingByPairingCode and enablePairingByQrCode both call enforceCallingOrSelfPermission(MANAGE_DEBUGGING). The pairing code is 6 SecureRandom digits. If Wi-Fi is not connected, the code logs 'Not connected to any wireless network. Not enabling adbwifi.' and resets the setting to 0. Working is not the same as safe: the CVE-2026-0073 check below shows this TLS path is probably exploitable on an unpatched Android 11 build.

checks.claim: 'Paired' just means the host key is in adb_keys, so a key you pre-seed (or accept with 'Always allow') also works for TLS connections without running adb pair.
checks.note: The code path supports it. adb_wifi.md defines paired as the host key being in /data/misc/adb/adb_keys or /adb_keys. Android 11 adbd_tls_verify_cert loops over adbd_auth_get_public_keys. libadbd_auth reads {"/adb_keys", "/data/misc/adb/adb_keys"} from disk on every call and compares each key with EVP_PKEY_cmp. I found no independent report of connecting to the TLS port without pairing, so this is untested. The same function contains the CVE-2026-0073 logic bug: it tests `if (EVP_PKEY_cmp(...))` for truthiness. The GUID / mDNS auto-connect detail is only partly supported: the doc mentions persist.adb.wifi.guid and auto-connect for previously paired devices.

checks.claim: Wireless debugging turns itself off when Wi-Fi drops or the BSSID changes. Trust is stored per BSSID. An untrusted network triggers SystemUI's WifiDebuggingActivity.
checks.note: The receiver logs 'Wifi disabled. Disabling adbwifi.', 'Network disconnected. Disabling adbwifi.', 'Unable to get the wifi ap's BSSID. Disabling adbwifi.' and 'Detected wifi network change. Disabling adbwifi.'. Trusted BSSIDs are stored as wifiAP entries in adb_temp_keys.xml. The Android 11 SystemUI manifest declares .wifi.WifiDebuggingActivity and .usb.UsbDebuggingActivity, both guarded by MANAGE_DEBUGGING. The framework starts the dialog through config_customAdbWifiNetworkConfirmationComponent, which a vendor can override. At boot, initAdbState reads persist.adb.tls_server.enable and systemReady writes it back to the setting; that it then switches off when Wi-Fi is not yet up is an inference from the not-connected branch. One cited source, mouldybread/adb-auto-enable, is an Android 14+ tool and does not support any of this; the AOSP code does. Separate BSSIDs per band is an inference.

checks.claim: Unauthenticated 5555 happens only on a debuggable or unlocked (orange) build with ro.adb.secure 0 or missing. The TCP listener comes from service./persist.adb.tcp.port, or falls back to 5555 when there is no USB FFS. Unlocking for Magisk can disable authentication by itself.
checks.note: main.cpp has `if (__android_log_is_debuggable() || device_unlocked) auth_required = GetBoolProperty("ro.adb.secure", false);`, where device_unlocked means ro.boot.verifiedbootstate == orange. auth.cpp sets the global `bool auth_required = true;` by default. A port property opens tcp and vsock listeners even when USB exists. The 5555 default only applies in the `else if (!is_usb)` branch. Missing detail: service.adb.listen_addrs overrides both. main.mk sets ro.adb.secure=1 only for 'user' builds and ro.debuggable=1 when enable_target_debugging. CVE-2026-30495 checks out: Optoma CinemaX P2, Android 8, network ADB without authentication plus su, CVSS 8.8 AV:A.

checks.claim: A Magisk system.prop line (or resetprop -n in post-fs-data) setting ro.adb.secure=1 takes effect before adbd starts.
checks.note: Magisk docs confirm that system.prop entries are 'loaded as system properties by resetprop', that post-fs-data is BLOCKING and runs before Zygote, and that setprop there deadlocks so resetprop -n must be used. They also confirm resetprop -p, -d/--delete and magisk --remove-modules. The docs do not say when system.prop is applied relative to post-fs-data, and I found no primary source that does. AOSP init.usb.rc starts adbd (class core, disabled) only through sys.usb.config property triggers, which get set at 'on boot', after post-fs-data, so the ordering is plausible on AOSP. Vendor .rc files on Allwinner builds are unverified. The research's post-boot getprop check and negative test are the right mitigation.

checks.claim: Lock-out risk: USB uses the same RSA auth. Pre-seed adb_keys and disable key expiry first. Escape routes: Magisk app, --remove-modules, Safe Mode (volume-down), HY300 flash button above HDMI with an A-A cable.
checks.note: Key expiry checks out. Keys from the user adb_keys file are added to the keystore by addUserKeysToKeyStore and then expire (`allowedTime != 0 && systemTime > connectionTime + allowedTime`). Value 0 means they never expire, and keys in the system /adb_keys file are exempt. The default is 604800000 ms (7 days since last use), per a secondary source and keystore.md. AOSP writes adb_keys with mode 0640, which matches the chmod. Amazon's Fire TV docs: 'The first time you run adb connect, Fire TV will show a screen that says "Allow USB debugging?"'. Magisk FAQ: hold volume-down before the boot animation for Safe Mode, or run magisk --remove-modules over ADB. androidpctv confirms an A-A cable plus a paperclip on the flash button above HDMI. Extra point: if no framework connects to adbd's socket, prompts are queued and never shown (adbd_auth.cpp), so pre-seeding is mandatory when the vendor SystemUI lacks the dialog. 'A_AUTH on every transport' was not shown verbatim in the files I fetched.

checks.claim: Legacy TCP ADB with RSA auth is authenticated but unencrypted. TLS wireless debugging is encrypted.
checks.note: The encryption half is right. adb_wifi.md: 'all traffic can be eavesdropped and open to MITM attacks' for tcpip, and the TLS socket 'opens communication with A_STLS'. The implied conclusion, that TLS is the safer upgrade, does not hold on this device. Android 11's TLS client check carries the CVE-2026-0073 authentication bypass (next check), so on an unpatched Android 11 build the encrypted TLS path is the less trustworthy one.

checks.claim: Enabling TLS wireless debugging (adb_wifi_enabled=1) on this Android 11 projector is a safe optional upgrade. Implied by the research's bottom line.
checks.note: CVE-2026-0073 (May 2026 bulletin, Critical, adbd Mainline component, A-469080888) is an adjacent-network shell-level bypass of wireless ADB mutual authentication with no user interaction. The fix commit 842d331f is titled 'Fix EVP_PKEY_cmp usage', with the message 'Not all non-zero values mean success.' Android 11's adbd_tls_verify_cert contains exactly `if (EVP_PKEY_cmp(known_evp.get(), evp_pkey.get()))`. BoringSSL returned -1 for mismatched key types until commit 3975388935 (January 2026). Per the Barghest write-up, an EC or Ed25519 client certificate therefore matches a stored RSA key, and the precondition is at least one RSA key in /data/misc/adb/adb_keys, which the plan pre-seeds. The bulletin lists only Android 14 to 16 because 11 is out of support, and this projector will never get the patched adbd APEX. Inference from code, not tested on the device. The legacy A_AUTH path on 5555 is a different code path, and Barghest says the vulnerable verifier is reached only when the device answers STLS.

checks.claim: LocalSend is a viable open-source way to send APKs but is buggy on Android TV and opens a LAN listener.
checks.note: F-Droid: Apache-2.0, 1.18.2 (August 2026), armeabi-v7a APK, Android 7.0+, REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES and run-at-startup, 'built and signed by the original developer'. Reproducibility is only linked, not stated. Protocol: port 53317, multicast 224.0.0.167, fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the cert, ?pin= option, and MITM is never mentioned. The download API uses plain HTTP. Issues #249 (OK button cannot accept transfers), #1264 (cannot control it with an Android TV remote; crash on Fire TV) and #3335 (APK does not install on an HY350max projector running Android TV 14) are all open with no fix. A 'Quick Save' auto-accept mode exists per a third-party page and could sidestep the OK-button bug, but it accepts unprompted transfers. Unverified on TV.

checks.claim: Material Files (GPL-3.0, F-Droid-signed, armeabi-v7a, Android 6+) reads FTP/SFTP/SMB/WebDAV shares and has the install-packages permission.
checks.note: F-Droid: GPL-3.0-or-later, 1.7.5 (September 2026), 'built and signed by F-Droid', arm64/armeabi-v7a/x86/x86_64, Android 6.0+, FTP/SFTP/SMB/WebDAV, REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES. Android TV is not mentioned, so remote usability is unknown.

checks.claim: Verify APKs with `apksigner verify --print-certs -v` (build-tools 24.0.3+) and compare the SHA-256 digest. Cross-check with F-Droid's signer-index.json or gpg using key 37D2 C987 ... 2E89. AirPlay Server 0.0.31 is developer-signed.
checks.note: The apksigner docs confirm 24.0.3+ and the --print-certs and -v options. The docs never mention a 'Verifies' output line, and the research itself marks the Java requirement as unsourced. ente's FAQ shows the 'Signer #1 certificate SHA-256 digest:' line in lowercase hex without colons. The F-Droid GPG fingerprint and the gpg --verify command are confirmed, as is signer-index.json signed via entry.json, the .jar and the .asc. AirPlay Server on F-Droid is 0.0.31 (August 2026), armeabi-v7a, 'built and signed by the original developer', GPL-3.0-only, Android 7.0+, but the page does not list the cert SHA-256. The GitHub releases have already moved on to v0.0.32 through v0.0.36 (16 to 19 October), so F-Droid lags. That GitHub and F-Droid builds carry the same cert has not been checked.

checks.claim: Refuse any third-party APK whose signer DN is the AOSP test DN, because the platform test key gives platform privileges.
checks.note: The README quote and the DN are confirmed. Platform-cert abuse is real: Google's APVI disclosure of leaked OEM platform certificates says an app signed with the platform cert can request android.uid.system. The DN test is weak, though. The same DN is used for all five test keys (testkey, platform, shared, media, cts_uicc_2021), and anyone can put that DN on their own self-made cert. The correct check compares the APK's cert SHA-256 with the device's platform cert (from the 'android' package) or with the published AOSP test-key digests.

checks.claim: A Magisk action.sh can toggle the ADB port. Because of the is_usb fallback, clearing the port does not close 5555; stopping adbd or turning USB debugging off does.
checks.note: Magisk: action.sh 'will be executed when user click the action button in Magisk app'. main.cpp confirms the fallback is gated on !is_usb. AOSP AdbService.stopAdbd() runs ctl.stop adbd only when both USB and Wi-Fi ADB are disabled, which supports 'turn USB debugging off'. Vendor behavior is untested.

checks.claim: DHCP reservation on the home router (listed as an open question, not researched).
checks.note: ASUS FAQ 1000906, 'How to manually assign LAN IP around the DHCP list': web GUI LAN > DHCP Server, manual assignment; app path Settings > LAN > IP Binding. The IP must be inside the DHCP pool. Menu names vary by firmware.

verify.corrected_bottom_line:
Keep classic TCP ADB on 5555 and enforce RSA authentication. The steps:
1. While unauthenticated root ADB still works, add the PC's adbkey.pub to /data/misc/adb/adb_keys (system:shell, mode 0640, restorecon). Then run `settings put global adb_allowed_connection_time 0` so the key never expires.
2. Set ro.adb.secure=1 with a removable Magisk module (system.prop).
3. Check after boot: `getprop ro.adb.secure` returns 1, a known key gets "device", and a fresh key gets "unauthorized". Port-scan the projector to see what is listening.
4. Run apksigner on every APK and compare the SHA-256 digest with F-Droid or the developer before `adb install`.

This is supported by the Android 11 adbd and framework source. Two warnings that show it actually works on this firmware (ro.adb.secure reads 1 and a fresh key gets "unauthorized") are the ones to watch.

Correction to the research: do NOT use the "optional TLS upgrade" on this device. Do not set adb_wifi_enabled=1, and make sure persist.adb.tls_server.enable stays 0. Android 11's adbd TLS check has the same EVP_PKEY_cmp bug that CVE-2026-0073 fixed only on Android 14 to 16. With a key already in adb_keys, which the plan adds, any device on the LAN could probably get a shell with no prompt. The projector will never receive the fixed adbd.

Legacy ADB is authenticated but not encrypted, and every unknown host pops an "Allow USB debugging?" dialog that one accidental OK press would approve forever. So it is better to keep ADB off between install sessions and confirm with a port scan that 5555 really closes. The PC's %USERPROFILE%\.android\adbkey is now a master key to the projector: anyone holding it can get a shell, so protect it.

The home router is on ASUS's end-of-life list and gets no more firmware. Use a DHCP reservation (LAN > DHCP Server, ASUS FAQ 1000906), keep 5555 out of any port forward, and turn off UPnP and remote WAN admin.

Fallbacks: the USB stick (zero network), or Material Files pulling from a read-only SMB share. LocalSend has open, unfixed Android TV remote bugs, including one HY-series projector where it would not install.

gaps.issue: CVE-2026-0073 on Android 11 has not been tested on the device. The conclusion rests on matching code plus the old BoringSSL return values. Also unknown: whether this firmware has persist.adb.tls_server.enable=1 or a vendor 'Network debugging' toggle that starts the TLS server or sets persist.adb.tcp.port. Check with getprop, port-scan for a random high port, and run `adb mdns services`.

The on-screen authorization prompt is attack surface. Any LAN host can trigger 'Allow USB debugging?'. It is unknown which button the dialog focuses by default with a TV remote, and whether the vendor SystemUI shows it at all. If the dialog is missing, prompts queue unanswered and the pre-seeded key is the only way in.

When Magisk loads system.prop compared with when adbd starts on this Allwinner H713 build is not documented. A vendor init .rc could start adbd before post-fs-data. Only the on-device getprop and negative tests can settle it.

The home router is end-of-life with no firmware updates. That makes the 'attacker already on the LAN' threat to unencrypted ADB, and to AirPlay's own listener, more realistic. A guest network with intranet access blocked would isolate the projector but also cut off ADB from the PC and AirPlay from the iPad. Not researched: UPnP, WPS and WAN-admin defaults on this model.

AirPlay Server: F-Droid has 0.0.31 while GitHub has v0.0.36 (19 Oct 2026). F-Droid's page does not list the signer SHA-256. Get it from F-Droid's signed index and confirm that GitHub release APKs carry the same cert, and that one of the 4 assets per release is armeabi-v7a or universal, before sideloading from GitHub.

Not covered by this research but central to the user's goal: whether Netflix and similar DRM apps will run on an unlocked-bootloader, Magisk-rooted, test-key Android 11 projector (Widevine level, Play Integrity, Netflix device certification). Unverified.
Whether a USB A-A ADB connection works for the initial key seeding on the HY320 is not verified. androidpctv only documents A-A for the flash tool.

research.bottom_line:
On these projectors most features come from vendor apps that are not malicious, and the hardware work happens below them, in native services, the HAL (hardware layer) and the kernel. A cleaned build can keep feature parity if it keeps one small group of vendor packages and deletes the malware and cast stack.

**Keep (and block their network access where you can):**
- HDMI: com.softwinner.awsource (source picker), com.softwinner.awlivetv (viewer) and com.softwinner.vis (input service).
- com.softwinner.awmanager (Allwinner system manager).
- Focus: com.hysd.vafocus and com.htc.closedialog. Both are harmless on the HY320, which has manual focus.
- com.htc.htcbluetoothremotecontrol, only if your remote is Bluetooth.
- AOSP Settings (com.android.settings on H713 builds), plus the native tvserver, display HAL and IR keylayout.
- The stock vendor launcher: keep it installed but not as the default home screen. On H713 it is the only interface for 4-corner keystone, flip/ceiling/rear and initial angle. Saved keystone values survive with it disabled; the vendor apps above need no internet.

**Replace with open-source apps:**
- Home screen: FLauncher (GPL-3.0) instead of the vendor launcher. Projectivy is the community default but proprietary.
- File manager: Material Files (GPL-3.0) instead of HiFileManager.
- Casting: AirPlay Server (io.github.jqssun.airplay, GPL-3.0) instead of the vendor AirPlay/toofifi/mphotool/samescreen stack.
- Keystone menu: a small app_process helper can call the display HAL directly, without the vendor launcher. This is proven only on an H726 / Android 14 unit.

**Delete:**
- Malware and OTA updaters: storeos, eventuploadservice, expandsdk, htcotaupdate, silentsdk, writesn, bootstart, screensaver SDK, the softwinner/L010/Rockchip updaters, hyk_test and huawei.connection.
- The whole toofifi/mphotool/samescreen cast stack, the factory menu, the memory cleaner and the office suite.
- The root binaries: qw, hotacksu and the setuid /system/bin/wifi.
- Keep com.softwinner.miracastReceiver only if you want Miracast from Windows (Win+K).

The biggest open question is the HY320's own package list. Run `pm list packages -f` on the projector and check which of the launcher variants it ships.

findings.claim: The HY320 has manual focus (lens ring) and auto keystone. The HY320F (electric focus) and HY320 Pro (autofocus) are different models.
findings.detail: Magcubic's comparison table lists HY320, HY320 mini and HY320NTV as 'Manual focus', keystone 'Auto', Android 11, AW869A Wi-Fi 6, which matches the product sheet. A search snippet from Magcubic's product page describes the HY320F as having electronic focus, and Magcubic's HY320 Pro setup guide describes autofocus. Versus.com claims motorised focus, but it conflicts with Magcubic and is old. com.hysd.vafocus ('autofocus motor control') therefore has no motor to drive on a plain HY320. It is harmless to keep and loses nothing if removed. Check the exact model name on the label, and note that one XDA post describes an RK3326-based HY320 Mini.

findings.claim: Keystone: the keystone screen lives in the vendor launcher APK, but the correction itself is done by the vendor display HAL / composer and stored in system properties. Another app can therefore drive it, and settings survive with the launcher disabled.
findings.detail: On an H726 / Android 14 HY300 Pro, the launcher sends 4 corner points to the HAL via a HIDL call: `vendor.display.config@1.0::IDisplayConfig` (instance 'default'), transaction 36. The values are saved as `persist.display.keystone_{ltx,lty,rtx,rty,lbx,lby,rbx,rby}` plus `keystone_zoom_h/v`, and the composer re-applies them at boot. The battleof3 project replaces the menu with `app_process` + keystone.dex (Keystone.java), tested only on build Projector.20260318.111759. On H713 HY300 Pro (LuminaOS), disabling com.htc.luminaos keeps 'basic keystone correction' but removes the advanced vertical-correction UI. That is consistent with the composer re-applying saved values, but the H713 HAL name and transaction number are not verified. Per the lolmam research, /oem/config.ini has flags `autoKeystone` (accelerometer-based) and `manualKeystone` (shows the 4-corner screen). Which process runs auto keystone from the g-sensor on H713 was not found; it may be the launcher (magcubicos has InitAngleActivity). Removing the launcher could stop auto keystone.

findings.claim: Projection settings (flip front/rear/ceiling, keystone, initial angle) are activities inside the vendor launcher package. The advice is to keep that package installed and switch the default home screen, not delete it.
findings.detail: com.htc.magcubicos contains CorrectionActivity (keystone), ProjectActivity (projection mode), InitAngleActivity and .activity.settings.*. The maximilian guide warns not to delete MagcubicOS.apk and to use `cmd package set-home-activity` for another launcher instead. com.htc.luminaos (HY300 Pro / L018) has `.activity.ProjectActivity` and the keystone UI. The manual describes Flip with 4 modes (front table/ceiling, back table/ceiling) under System Settings. The lower-level mechanism for flip (property, HAL or sysfs) was NOT found. Assume the vendor UI is needed to change it, and that the value then persists. well0nez marks magcubicos/luminaos 'Keep if you need projector alignment tools'. battleof3 disables magcubicos only after a working keystone replacement.

findings.claim: Launcher variants: com.htc.luminaos, com.htc.magcubicos and com.htc.htclauncherhighenglishd08. The last one is labelled malicious, the other two are vendor UI with analytics.
findings.detail: micha102 and the probonopd gist say htclauncherhighenglishd08 contacts shortx.srafx.com (a video-shorts site) and imasdk.googleapis.com, and should be removed only after installing another launcher plus an HDMI shortcut. The micha102 README says it was generated with DeepSeek. maximilian-sh lists it as malicious ('referenced, delete if present'). battleof3 says magcubicos bundles Baidu analytics but keeps it until a replacement keystone works. The guides warn to install a replacement launcher BEFORE disabling the stock one, or you are left with no home screen and must reflash. Which variant the HY320 ships: not found.

findings.claim: HDMI input is handled by Allwinner (softwinner) packages, not by the malicious set: com.softwinner.awsource (picker), com.softwinner.awlivetv (viewer) and com.softwinner.vis (input service, HdmiInputService), sitting on the Android TV-input framework.
findings.detail: `am start -n com.softwinner.awlivetv/.MainActivity` opens HDMI on H713 (gist, micha102). On H726, battleof3 adds `--es input_source HDMI2`, because the driver registers 3 inputs and only one is wired; check with `dumpsys tv_input | grep HdmiInputService`. Projectivy's 'Inputs' entries cannot open HDMI, because the firmware does not handle the standard TV-passthrough intent. Use awsource or an explicit awlivetv shortcut instead. Removing any of the three breaks HDMI. No source reports network behaviour for them.

findings.claim: Picture and sound settings are carried out by the native tvserver and picture-quality (PQ) config files, with screens in the vendor settings or launcher UI. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth use the stock AOSP Settings, which has no launcher icon.
findings.detail: battleof3 (H726): the vendor Picture and Focus screens live in TV Settings (com.android.tv.settings/.MainSettings). Picture settings persist only if tvserver can write /oem (panel_config.ini rules). On H713 HY310/L018, Settings is com.android.settings with no launcher intent-filter; open it with `am start -n com.android.settings/.Settings` or a launcher shortcut. config.ini flags `network`/`bluetooth` control those menus. The setup wizard (com.htc.htcsetup_wizard_*, HTC_Wizard_QZ) should be disabled only after `device_provisioned` and `user_setup_complete` are both 1. Exact H713 picture-settings package: not found.

findings.claim: Remote control: IR is decoded by the kernel (sunxi-ir, rc_map_sunxi) and mapped through a keylayout file. The Bluetooth remote uses the vendor app com.htc.htcbluetoothremotecontrol, which should be kept if the remote is Bluetooth.
findings.detail: H713 dmesg shows 'Registered IR keymap rc_map_sunxi', device sunxi-ir at .../7040000.s_cir. On H726 the keylayout is /oem/usr/keylayout/sunxi-ir.kl. The input and cast buttons send vendor keycodes PRJ_AIRPLAY (643) and PRJ_MIRACAST (642), and the mouse key sends 10009. Once the vendor cast apps are gone, battleof3 comments those lines out and remaps the buttons with a getevent script. maximilian lists sunxi-ir, cir_param (DTB) and ble_remote/bt_remote as needed for the remote. battleof3 keeps com.htc.htcbluetoothremotecontrol ('Remote service'). Netflix: com.android.nfx is a Netflix D-pad accessibility helper with no INTERNET permission on one H713 firmware (florentine). On H726 a vendor hook in services.jar force-enables it, and battleof3 removed it. Test Netflix navigation before deleting nfx.

findings.claim: Vendor screen mirroring is all suspect or phone-home code and can be replaced: com.android.toofifi, com.toofifi.lineserver, com.toofifi.miracast, com.mphotool.usbcastserver/USBCastServer/iOSUsbCastServer/htc_cast, com.mphotool.airplay (AirPlayServer), com.mphotool.dlna (FtDlnaNoUi) and com.htc.samescreen.
findings.detail: well0nez says toofifi phones home to China and that AirPlay ports 7000/7002/9528 and Audio HAL port 14035 are bound to 0.0.0.0. florentine reports phone-home to server.mphotool.com:8680 and log uploads. maximilian reports that mphotool AirPlay/DLNA need activation from server.mphotool.com, stored in `settings global ft_activated_data`, and that samescreen opens the cloud session. All of these are user-space apps, not HALs. For the iPad, use io.github.jqssun.airplay (GPL-3.0, Android 7+, H.264/H.265 mirroring, same subnet, no DRM). Disable the vendor AirPlay so the iPad sees only one receiver; this is my inference. com.softwinner.miracastReceiver (Allwinner) is the only path for Windows Win+K / Miracast; no phone-home is reported for it, but none was ruled out either.

findings.claim: The file manager, media viewer, memory cleaner, screensaver and office apps are plain vendor bloat or SDK hosts, and open-source apps replace them.
findings.detail: The H713 /product/app listing includes HiFileManager, Gallery2 (AOSP), ClearMemory, ScreenSaverQZ, HtcOfficeSuite, Browser2, BluetoothSpeaker, LatinIME, webview and ModuleMetadata. battleof3 disables com.htc.clearmemory and com.mobisystems.office (it intercepts content:// links), and removes com.htc.screensaver, the host for the com.hotack.screensaversdk payload. Material Files (GPL-3.0, Android 5+, SMB/FTP/WebDAV, root) can replace HiFileManager. Keep webview (System WebView, which apps need), LatinIME and ModuleMetadata. BluetoothSpeaker (projector as a Bluetooth speaker) is optional; nothing malicious is reported for it.

findings.claim: The boot animation and splash screen are plain files on the /oem partition, with no app behind them.
findings.detail: /oem/media/bootanimation.zip (stored zip, desc.txt + frames) takes priority over /system/media/bootanimation.zip, and /oem/bootlogo.bmp (1280x720, 24-bit) is the U-Boot splash. /oem/customer.prop overrides build.prop. It sets names such as ro.miracast.name and an OTA channel. Deleting packages does not affect the boot animation.

findings.claim: Delete the confirmed malicious, updater and factory packages and the root binaries. None of them provides a user-facing feature.
findings.detail: Malicious: com.htc.storeos (dropper), com.htc.eventuploadservice (telemetry and remote admin), com.htc.expandsdk (ads and persistence), com.hotack.silentsdk (RAT/proxy), com.hotack.writesn, com.htc.bootstart, com.htc.htcotaupdate, and com.me.cash5 plus proxy plugins. OTA updaters: com.softwinner.update, UpdateService_L010, /system/app/Update/Update.apk and android.rockchip.update.service. Factory and test: com.htc.hyk_test and com.softwinner.tv.factorymenu. Also com.huawei.connection. Root binaries: /system/bin/qw (su daemon), /system/xbin/hotacksu, and the setuid /system/bin/wifi. On H713, silentsdk lives in /system, so it can only be disabled until /system is edited. The vendor scripts appsdisable and gmsopt disable Google boot receivers, which matters if you install Google apps.

findings.claim: The firmware's network-side tweaks need fixing for a clean internet-connected setup: the connectivity-check and NTP servers point at China-hosted endpoints, and the vendor overlay cannot be disabled.
findings.detail: Found on H726. Allwinner compiled www.google.cn/generate_204 into NetworkStack resources, and the vendor overlay repeats it. battleof3 ships its own overlay and sets `settings put global ntp_server` and the `captive_portal_*` URLs. Not verified on H713, so check what the HY320 does. The same applies to H726 'Lumina Go' firmware, which exposes an unauthenticated LAN control API on TCP 8899 (with factory-reset commands). If it exists on the HY320, it argues for keeping the vendor launcher blocked from the network or removing it.

findings.claim: Blocking network access per app for the vendor packages you keep needs root and a UID-based firewall. Apps that share the system UID cannot be isolated this way.
findings.detail: AFWall+ (GPL-3.0, requires root, Android 5 to 14+) blocks apps individually, but its documentation does not cover shared UIDs. The firmware is signed with AOSP test keys, and vendor services listen as UID 1000 (Kavan00). Any kept vendor app that uses sharedUserId android.uid.system can only be removed, not firewalled. This is an inference: check with `dumpsys package <pkg> | grep userId=`.

findings.claim: Two launcher replacements: Projectivy Launcher is the community default but proprietary; FLauncher is a GPL-3.0 open-source option.
findings.detail: Projectivy (com.spocky.projengmenu) is used by battleof3, maximilian and the androidpctv HY320 clean firmware. AlternativeTo lists it as freemium and proprietary, and a Privacy Guides post notes it requires an accessibility-service permission. FLauncher (GitLab flauncher/flauncher, GPL-3.0, Flutter) handles sideloaded non-TV apps; its maintenance in 2026 was not confirmed. Whichever launcher you use needs shortcuts to awlivetv/awsource, Settings and the vendor keystone/projection activities. A Home Assistant project reports that the vendor launcher starts before user launchers; its ADB Boot helper sends HOME so the chosen launcher comes to the front.

open_questions: Exact HY320 package set. Which launcher does it ship: luminaos, magcubicos or htclauncherhighenglishd08? Is com.hysd.vafocus present on a manual-focus unit? Answer with `pm list packages -f` and `ls /product/app /system/app /vendor/app /system/priv-app` on the projector.

Does the H713 / Android 11 build use the same vendor.display.config@1.0::IDisplayConfig transaction 36 and the persist.display.keystone_* properties? Check with `getprop | grep -i keystone` and `lshal | grep display.config` before relying on a launcher-free keystone helper.
Which component does auto keystone from the accelerometer (config.ini autoKeystone), and does it keep working once the vendor launcher is disabled? Not found; test it on the device.
How flip/ceiling/rear projection is stored (property, HAL call or tvserver)? Not found. Run `getprop` before and after changing it in the vendor UI to find out.
Do kept vendor apps (awsource/awlivetv/vis/awmanager/vafocus/BT remote) share android.uid.system? That decides whether a UID firewall can isolate them or whether they must be trusted.
Does the HY320 firmware hardcode China-hosted connectivity-check/NTP endpoints (as found on H726) or expose the Lumina Go port-8899 API? Check with `netstat -tlnp` and `cmd overlay list`.
Is com.android.nfx present, and is it needed for D-pad navigation in Netflix on this build? Is the fingerprint spoofed (ADT-3, as on one H713 firmware)? Both affect Netflix behaviour after cleanup.
Does io.github.jqssun.airplay ship an armeabi-v7a build that runs on a 32-bit H713 userspace? Its README does not list ABIs.

checks.claim: 1. The HY320 has manual focus and auto keystone; the HY320F (electric focus) and HY320 Pro (autofocus) are different models, so com.hysd.vafocus has nothing to drive on a plain HY320.
checks.note: Magcubic's compare table lists HY320 and HY320 mini as 'Manual focus', keystone 'Auto', Android 11, AW869A. The HY320F page says 'electronic focus' and auto vertical keystone, but it is an H726 / Android 14 unit, a different platform from the user's. The HY320 Pro guide says it 'supports automatic focusing' and runs Android 14. The global sources spec sheet says H713 with manual focus. 'Loses nothing if vafocus is removed' is an inference: well0nez marks vafocus 'Keep (autofocus motor control, hardware-related)'. The XDA RK3326 thread returned 403, so I could not check it.

checks.claim: 2. Keystone correction is done by the vendor display HAL/composer and stored in persist.display.keystone_* properties, so another app can drive it and settings survive with the launcher disabled.
checks.note: Confirmed for H726 / Android 14 only. Keystone.java uses HAL 'vendor.display.config@1.0::IDisplayConfig', instance 'default', TRANSACT_SET_KEYSTONE = 36, and the 8 persist.display.keystone_* properties plus zoom_h/v. battleof3 enables the helper only on build 20260318.111759, and the code itself has no build check. On H713, the probonopd gist (HY300 Pro+, LuminaOS) says 'basic keystone correction still works, but there is no UI anymore for the more advanced vertical correction'. That is consistent with the claim, but it does not show whether saved values or auto keystone are what survives. No source shows the H713 HAL name, the transaction number or the property names: searches for persist.display.keystone found nothing outside battleof3. The config.ini autoKeystone/manualKeystone flags are confirmed in lolmam CUSTOMIZATION.md. Which process runs auto keystone from the accelerometer on H713: not found.

checks.claim: 3. Projection settings (flip, keystone, initial angle) are activities in the vendor launcher, so keep it installed and only change the default home activity.
checks.note: maximilian (HY350 Max, H726) confirms: keystone is CorrectionActivity and projection mode is ProjectActivity inside com.htc.magcubicos. It says not to delete MagcubicOS.apk and to use 'cmd package set-home-activity'. The gist shows com.htc.luminaos/.activity.ProjectActivity on H713, and well0nez marks both launchers 'Keep if you need alignment tools'. Not verified: InitAngleActivity, '.activity.settings.*', and the 4-mode Flip menu in the manuals.plus manual (403). Also not verified for the HY320's own launcher. Caveat from schaumann (H726): the vendor launcher is direct-boot-aware and starts before the user's launcher even when another app holds the HOME role, and changing persist.sys.homePackage has no effect. Changing the default home therefore may not be enough by itself.

checks.claim: 4. The launcher variants are luminaos, magcubicos and htclauncherhighenglishd08; the last is malicious and the other two are vendor UI with analytics. Install a replacement launcher before disabling the stock one.
checks.note: micha102 and the gist describe htclauncherhighenglishd08 as malware contacting shortx.srafx.com and imasdk.googleapis.com. The micha102 README does end with 'Readme generated with Deepseek'. maximilian lists it under 'referenced, but not preinstalled', as a malicious launcher. battleof3 lists Baidu analytics (hmma.baidu.com) in magcubicos. Analytics in luminaos: no source found. Which launcher the HY320 ships: not found. The androidpctv HY300/HY320/L018 clean firmware replaces the launcher with Projectivy and does not name the stock one.

checks.claim: 5. HDMI input is handled by com.softwinner.awsource, awlivetv and vis on the TV-input framework. Projectivy 'Inputs' cannot open it, and removing any of the three breaks HDMI.
checks.note: battleof3 lists awsource (source picker), awlivetv (viewer) and vis (HDMI input service) as Keep. It says the driver registers three HDMI inputs and only one is wired (check with dumpsys tv_input | grep HdmiInputService). It says Projectivy's Inputs entries cannot open HDMI because nothing on the firmware handles the standard TV-passthrough intent. remote-buttons.sh launches awlivetv with '--es input_source HDMI2', described as the same intent awsource sends. The gist confirms 'am start -n com.softwinner.awlivetv/.MainActivity' on H713. 'Removing any of the three breaks HDMI' is an inference that no source tests.

checks.claim: 6. Picture and sound come from tvserver plus PQ configs, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth use AOSP Settings with no launcher icon, and the setup wizard should be disabled only after device_provisioned and user_setup_complete are both 1.
checks.note: Confirmed: on H726 the Picture and Focus screens are in com.android.tv.settings/.MainSettings (no icon), and tvserver needs /oem write access (panel_config.ini sepolicy rules, not shown). On H713 HY310/L018, com.android.settings has no launcher intent-filter and opens via am start (well0nez). The config.ini network/bluetooth flags are confirmed. The device_provisioned/user_setup_complete rule and com.htc.htcsetup_wizard_d55 are confirmed. Not found: 'HTC_Wizard_QZ' and the H713 picture-settings package.

checks.claim: 7. IR is decoded in the kernel (sunxi-ir, rc_map_sunxi) and mapped by a keylayout, the BT remote needs com.htc.htcbluetoothremotecontrol, and com.android.nfx is a Netflix D-pad helper with no INTERNET permission.
checks.note: H713 dmesg in the gist shows 'Registered IR keymap rc_map_sunxi' at 7040000.s_cir. On H726 the keylayout is /oem/usr/keylayout/sunxi-ir.kl: key 643 PRJ_AIRPLAY (scancode 0x93), key 642 PRJ_MIRACAST (0x98), and the 'key 64[23]' lines are commented out to remap. The mouse button is Linux key 365, and the script notes that 'vendor keycode (10009)' maps to KEYCODE_UNKNOWN on injection, so the 10009 detail is roughly right. battleof3 keeps htcbluetoothremotecontrol as 'Remote service'. florentine (H713M, Android 11) describes nfx in /system/priv-app/NFXAccessibility, 'no INTERNET permission at all', active only while com.netflix.mediaclient is in front, and keeps it. battleof3 removes nfx and ytb on H726 because a services.jar hook force-enables them. Since the user wants Netflix, keeping nfx is the better default.

checks.claim: 8. The vendor cast stack (toofifi, mphotool, samescreen) is phone-home code and can be replaced by io.github.jqssun.airplay for the iPad. miracastReceiver is the only path for Win+K.

Resolves the open question: F-Droid lists armeabi-v7a builds (0.0.29 to 0.0.31, Aug 2026), and GitHub has releases up to v0.0.36 (19 Oct).

checks.claim: 9. The file manager, gallery, cleaner, screensaver and office apps are bloat or SDK hosts, and Material Files can replace HiFileManager.
checks.note: The gist's /product/app listing includes HiFileManager, Gallery2, ClearMemory, ScreenSaverQZ, HtcOfficeSuite, Browser2, BluetoothSpeaker and CloseDialog_QZ. battleof3 disables clearmemory and mobisystems.office (it 'claims every content:// link') and removes com.htc.screensaver, the host for com.hotack.screensaversdk. Material Files README: GPL-3.0, Android 5.0+, FTP/SFTP/SMB/WebDAV, root. It says nothing about Android TV or D-pad support, or about installing APKs, so remote-only use and 'install from file manager' are untested. No source reports malicious behaviour for HiFileManager or Gallery2, and none clears them either.

checks.claim: 10. The boot animation and splash are plain files on /oem, and /oem/customer.prop overrides build.prop.
checks.note: lolmam: /oem/media/bootanimation.zip 'Takes priority over /system/media/bootanimation.zip', bootlogo.bmp is a 1280x720 24-bit BMP drawn by U-Boot, customer.prop overrides /system/build.prop, ro.miracast.name=Projector-Cast, and the OTA channel is persist.sys.Channel. A cleaned unit stays trivially rootable until /oem permissions and customer.prop are locked down.

checks.claim: 11. Delete the malicious, updater and factory packages and the root binaries (qw, hotacksu, setuid /system/bin/wifi); none provides a user-facing feature, and silentsdk lives in /system on H713.
checks.note: Confirmed: Kavan00 (H713) names storeos, silentsdk, eventuploadservice, expandsdk, bootstart, htcotaupdate, com.me.cash5 and the proxy plugins, plus /system/bin/qw. well0nez names huawei.connection, hyk_test and android.rockchip.update.service. battleof3 names softwinner.update and factorymenu. The gist shows UpdateService_L010 and /system/app/Update/Update.apk. lolmam documents /system/bin/wifi as 4755 SUID root, a vendor su that grants root only from the UART console. well0nez confirms appsdisable 'disables all Google boot receivers including Play Protect on first boot'. Weak or wrong parts: (a) 'silentsdk lives in /system on H713' is not supported. Kavan00 says StoreOS downloaded it at runtime on its unit and a different analysis found it preinstalled, and well0nez gives no path. (b) hotacksu is documented only on H726 (maximilian). (c) maximilian lists writesn as a 'proxy helper' that is referenced but not preinstalled. (d) The updaters are a user feature (firmware updates); removing them is right but it is a tradeoff. (e) gmsopt's role is not documented.

checks.claim: 12. The connectivity-check and NTP endpoints point at China, and the Lumina Go API on port 8899 is unauthenticated, which argues for blocking or removing the vendor launcher.
checks.note: Confirmed on H726: Allwinner built www.google.cn/generate_204 into NetworkStack resources, so battleof3 ships an overlay and sets ntp_server to 'time.android.com|time.google.com' in place of ntp.ntsc.ac.cn and ntp.aliyun.com. schaumann (HY300 Pro+, H726, Android 14): Lumina Go v3.0.0 runs a web remote on 8899, 'no auth, LAN only', with 130 commands, and the integration blocks FACTORY_RESET and CLR_DATA. Unsupported: that the vendor launcher serves 8899, since schaumann does not name the package. Nothing found for H713.

checks.claim: 13. Per-app network blocking needs root and a UID firewall, and kept vendor apps that share android.uid.system can only be removed, not firewalled.
checks.note: AFWall+ README: GPL-3.0, root required, Android 5 to 14+. It does not mention shared UIDs. Android docs: apps with the same sharedUserId share one Linux UID. battleof3: 'Most vendor apps run with the shared system UID, so each one effectively holds system powers.' A UID firewall therefore cannot separate them. The claim overstates one point: you can firewall UID 1000 as a whole. That would also cut system_server, which runs as UID 1000, and the shared apps still hold system privileges, so firewalling is not real isolation. Check each app with dumpsys package.

checks.claim: 14. Projectivy is the community default but proprietary and needs an accessibility service; FLauncher is the GPL-3.0 option.
checks.note: battleof3 and the androidpctv HY320 clean firmware use Projectivy (com.spocky.projengmenu). Its GitHub repo (spocky/miproja1) holds only configs and an issue tracker, with no source code, so it is effectively closed. I could not verify the AlternativeTo 'freemium/proprietary' citation: the page fetched was the alternatives list. Wrong as stated: the developer's listing calls the accessibility service optional, used for remote shortcuts and foreground-app detection. The Privacy Guides post is a single unanswered question. FLauncher: the GitLab original is GPL-3.0 with no visible recent dates. osrosal's GPL-3.0 fork lists 'Support for non-TV (sideloaded) apps', and its last release is 2025.07.001 (27 Jul 2025), so maintenance is uncertain in 2026. schaumann's helper sends HOME at boot because the vendor launcher comes up first.

verify.corrected_bottom_line:
The package-level map largely holds up, but most of the detailed evidence (the keystone HAL, the shared-UID note, google.cn/NTP, the 8899 API, the services.jar nfx hook) comes from H726 / Android 14 units, not the user's H713 / Android 11 HY320. Treat those details as hypotheses to check on the device.

**Keep:**
- HDMI: com.softwinner.awsource, awlivetv and vis.
- com.softwinner.awmanager.
- com.htc.htcbluetoothremotecontrol, if the remote is Bluetooth.
- AOSP Settings: com.android.settings on H713, which has no icon.
- com.android.nfx: on H713 it has no INTERNET permission, and it exists for D-pad control of the Netflix app the user wants.
- The stock launcher, installed but not default. It holds the keystone and projection screens, and on H713 it may also run auto keystone. Removing or replacing it is only safe once `getprop`, `lshal` and tests prove keystone and flip survive without it.
- Note: vafocus and closedialog ('focus service' on H726) have no confirmed role on a manual-focus HY320.

**Delete:**
- The documented malware and updaters.
- The toofifi/mphotool/samescreen cast stack.
- qw, hotacksu (if present) and the setuid /system/bin/wifi.
- miracastReceiver too, unless Win+K is wanted.

**Replace:**
- Casting: AirPlay Server (io.github.jqssun.airplay). F-Droid lists armeabi-v7a builds, so it should install on the 32-bit userspace.
- Launcher: Projectivy (closed source; its accessibility service is optional) or the osrosal FLauncher fork (GPL-3.0, last release July 2025).
- File manager: Material Files (GPL-3.0, SMB/FTP/WebDAV client). It has no documented D-pad support.

**Corrections:**
- 'silentsdk lives in /system on H713' is unsupported.
- A UID firewall cannot isolate apps that share the system UID. Firewalling UID 1000 as a whole also cuts system_server, so treat kept system-UID apps as trusted or remove them.
- /oem is world-writable, and customer.prop overrides build.prop, so it can re-enable root. It must be locked down for the device to be 'safe on Wi-Fi'.

**Netflix:** This HY320 has no Netflix certification. Only the HY320 NTV variant is sold as Netflix-licensed. Expect the sideloaded mobile app at about SD (Widevine L3). That is a hardware and licensing limit that cleanup cannot fix.

gaps.issue: Netflix quality and availability. Only the separate HY320 NTV (Whale OS) is sold as Netflix-licensed. The androidpctv review of the related HY310 says it 'lacks certification for paid streaming platforms', and uncertified L3 devices are capped at about 480p. Rooting or unlocking may also change Play Store visibility. Check with DRM Info and `getprop ro.build.fingerprint` (one H713 build spoofs Google ADT-3) before promising Netflix. Plan for the mobile APK plus nfx for D-pad, or an HDMI stick if HD is required.

Safe APK install from the PC over Wi-Fi (user's q8) is not covered. Stock 5555 is 'ADB without authentication' as root (Kavan00). AOSP user builds normally force RSA auth, so the vendor changed adbd or its properties, and how is unknown. Android docs say pairing-code Wireless debugging needs Android 13+ on TV. The HY320 ships phone Settings (com.android.settings), so the Android 11 Wireless debugging toggle may still exist, but this is unverified. Steps: check `getprop ro.adb.secure` and whether a new PC triggers the RSA 'allow' prompt. If not, keep ADB off or block 5555, and use a USB stick or an SMB share opened in Material Files.

Auto keystone (the HY320's advertised keystone mode) on H713: which process reads the g-sensor and applies it, and whether it survives disabling the launcher, was not found. The only H713 data point says 'basic keystone correction still works' with LuminaOS disabled, and it is ambiguous. Flip/ceiling storage was also not found.

The vendor launcher may come back to the front at boot even when another launcher is default: it is direct-boot-aware, and persist.sys.homePackage is ignored (seen on H726). Plan for a HOME-sending boot helper or an equivalent Magisk service.

/oem is world-writable, and customer.prop overrides build.prop, so any app or shell can set ro.debuggable / ro.secure=0 for root. The research's cleanup list does not include remounting /oem or fixing its permissions and cleaning customer.prop.

Router: ASUS lists the home router as end-of-life, with no more firmware updates, and no VLAN or IoT-segment feature was found for it. Guest-network isolation (the usual containment) would break AirPlay, which needs the iPad on the same subnet, and PC-to-projector ADB/SMB. The 'isolate the projector' advice from well0nez and maximilian therefore conflicts with the user's AirPlay and Wi-Fi APK goals. The safe setup has to rely on on-device cleanup plus router-level domain/IP blocking where possible. Whether this router has an 'Access Intranet' guest toggle, DNS filtering or AiProtection is unverified.
Whether Material Files can be driven by the remote (D-pad) and can hand APKs to the package installer is undocumented. Test it, or keep a TV-friendly fallback for file browsing.

The HY320's actual package set is still unknown (launcher variant, whether vafocus or closedialog exist, whether silentsdk is preinstalled or downloaded, and its path). Every keep/delete decision depends on `pm list packages -f` from this unit.
